lede: One of the very first surahs. They had begun to call him a madman, and the reply came by an oath on the pen and all that is written with it: you are not mad — and then praise such as no man was ever given, in one line.

names.name: al-Qalam
names.note: After the oath in its first ayah: by the pen, and what they write.

names.name: Nūn
names.note: The single letter it opens with — one of the twenty-nine surahs that begin with letters, and on the traditional order the first of them to be revealed. Ibn Kathīr heads it Sūrat Nūn, and al-Qurṭubī Nūn wa-l-Qalam.

revelation.verdict: Makkan — with a passage some held Madinan
revelation.detail: Ibn al-Jawzī records agreement that it is Makkan, apart from what is related from Ibn ʿAbbās and Qatādah: that the parable of the owners of the garden, ayat 17–33, came down in Madinah. Al-Qurṭubī gives the same report in more detail, and gives it as Makkan in the saying of al-Ḥasan, ʿIkrimah, ʿAṭāʾ and Jābir. The traditional order places it second, directly after the opening of al-ʿAlaq.
revelation.when: The very beginning of the mission, when the first response of Quraysh was to call him mad

evidence.quote: سُورَةُ القَلَمِ وَهِيَ مَكِّيَّةٌ كُلُّها بِإجْماعِهِمْ إلّا ما حُكِيَ عَنِ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ وقَتادَةَ أنَّ فِيها مِنَ المَدَنِيِّ قَوْلَهُ تَعالى: ﴿إنّا بَلَوْناهُمْ﴾ إلى قَوْلِهِ تَعالى: ﴿لَوْ كانُوا يَعْلَمُونَ
مَكِّيَّةٌ فِي قَوْلِ الْحَسَنِ وَعِكْرِمَةَ وَعَطَاءٍ وَجَابِرٍ

attested.quote: أخْرَجَ النَّحّاسُ، وابْنُ مَرْدُويَهْ، والبَيْهَقِيُّ، عَنِ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ قالَ: نَزَلَتْ سُورَةُ ﴿ن والقَلَمِ﴾ بِمَكَّةَ
attested.says: Ibn ʿAbbās: it came down in Makkah. Recorded by al-Naḥḥās, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqī.

attested.quote: هي مَكِّيَّةٌ في قَوْلِ الحَسَنِ، وعِكْرِمَةَ، وعَطاءٍ، وجابِرٍ
attested.says: Makkan, in the saying of al-Ḥasan, ʿIkrimah, ʿAṭāʾ and Jābir ibn Zayd.

setting: For forty years the people of Makkah had known Muḥammad ﷺ as the most truthful and level-headed man among them. Then he told them that an angel had come to him with words from the Lord of the worlds, and they needed an explanation that did not involve believing him. The first one they found was majnūn — possessed.

This surah meets that word in its second ayah and returns to it in its second-last. In between it says three things to him. You are not mad. You will have a reward that never ends. And you are upon a tremendous character. When ʿĀʾishah was later asked what his character was, she answered with a sentence that points straight back here: his character was the Qurʾan.

It then turns to the men behind the slander and tells him not to give way to them: “They wish you would soften, so that they would soften.” One of them is described so exactly — the habitual swearer, the scandal-monger, the one who blocks every good, coarse and base-born — that the commentators give his name; most say al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīrah.{reported}

And it tells a story for people who think their wealth is their own doing: the owners of a garden who vowed to harvest it at dawn before the poor could come, and did not say “if Allah wills”. They found it black and bare. Quraysh, too, had been given a garden.
aim: To make manifest the Prophet’s ﷺ knowledge and character, in support of him after the idolaters’ insolence towards him.
themes: The character of the Prophet ﷺ
The Day the shin is laid bare

outline.title: The oath, and the answer
outline.summary: Nūn. By the pen and what they write: you are not, by the favour of your Lord, a madman. Yours is a reward unfailing, and you are of a tremendous character (68:4). You will see, and they will see, which of you is the one afflicted.

outline.title: Do not give way to them
outline.summary: Do not obey the deniers; they would love you to compromise, so that they might. And do not obey any worthless swearer, slanderer, carrier of tales, hinderer of good, transgressor, sinner — coarse, and besides all that, base — because he has wealth and sons. When Our ayat are recited to him he says, “Tales of the ancients.” We shall brand him on the snout.

outline.title: The owners of the garden
outline.summary: We have tested them as We tested the owners of the garden, who swore to pick its fruit in the morning and made no exception. A visitation from your Lord came upon it while they slept. They set out early, whispering that no poor man should get in — and when they saw it they said, “We are lost… no, we are deprived.” The most balanced of them said, “Did I not tell you — why do you not glorify Allah?” Such is the punishment; and the punishment of the Hereafter is greater.

outline.title: Are the two alike?
outline.summary: For the mindful there are gardens of delight with their Lord. Shall We treat those who submit like the guilty? What is the matter with you — how do you judge? On the Day the shin is laid bare and they are called to prostrate, they will not be able to; they used to be called to it when they were sound. So leave Me with those who deny this discourse: We shall lead them on by degrees from where they do not know.

outline.title: Be patient
outline.summary: So be patient for your Lord’s decision, and do not be like the Companion of the Fish, who cried out in distress. Those who disbelieve would almost strike you down with their looks when they hear the Reminder, and they say, “He is mad.” But it is nothing other than a reminder to all the worlds.

keyAyah.why: The Qurʾan’s own description of the one it was sent down to.

virtues.text: Saʿd ibn Hishām asked ʿĀʾishah: “Tell me about the character of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.” She said: “Do you not read the Qurʾan?” He said: “Yes.” She said: “The character of the Prophet of Allah ﷺ was the Qurʾan.”
virtues.arabic: فَإِنَّ خُلُقَ نَبِيِّ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم كَانَ الْقُرْآنَ

virtues.text: On “the Day the shin is laid bare”: “Our Lord will uncover His shin, and every believing man and woman will prostrate to Him. There will remain those who used to prostrate in the world to be seen and heard of: they will go to prostrate, and their backs will become a single plate.”

before: Al-Mulk ended with what the Prophet ﷺ was to say to those who denied him. Al-Qalam opens with what his Lord says of him.
after: Al-Qalam warned that the punishment of the Hereafter is greater. Al-Ḥāqqah names that reality and unfolds it.
